items.text: LW-PET NATURAL is an innovative lightweight 3D printing filament designed for applications where weight reduction is essential.
This makes LW-PET suitable for both technical lightweight components and larger creative prints where reduced part weight provides an advantage.
The combination of lower weight and increased flexibility makes LW-PET particularly suitable for thin-walled structures and applications where conventional rigid materials would add unnecessary mass.
LW-PET is particularly suitable for applications where every gram matters .
Drones and RC components can benefit from reduced mass, while the adjustable density and flexibility make the material interesting for helmet padding and other lightweight structures.
The material is also suitable for creative applications such as vases and lampshades .
LW-PET NATURAL is a lightweight 3D printing filament developed for significant weight reduction.
Thanks to minimal warping, easy printability and a wide processing window , LW-PET is ideal for drones, RC applications, helmet padding, vases, lampshades and other lightweight parts.
It uses temperature-controlled expansion to produce lightweight, low-density parts.
As the density decreases, LW-PET also becomes more flexible .
This allows designers to adjust the behaviour of a printed part by controlling the degree of expansion.
LW-PET NATURAL is designed for easy and reliable printing .
Its lightweight construction, minimal warping and characteristic expanded appearance can provide both functional and aesthetic benefits.
As the material expands, printed parts become lighter and more flexible.
exhibits minimal warping
Its wide processing window and very low tendency to warp make it suitable for larger models and geometries where dimensional accuracy is important.
Warping: Very low
The material is exceptionally easy to print, exhibits minimal warping and offers a wide processing window.

The active foaming process begins at approximately 210°C , after which expansion gradually increases up to around 260°C . As the printing temperature rises, the material expands during extrusion and forms a lower-density structure.
Settings such as temperature and material flow can therefore be used to influence the final density and weight of a printed part.
Lower temperatures produce less expansion and denser parts, while increased foaming can be used to create significantly lighter structures.
It can be processed at relatively low temperatures while remaining printable at temperatures of up to 300°C .
Lower temperatures can be used for denser parts, while higher temperatures activate more expansion and reduce part weight.

items.text: LW-PET FLEX NATURAL is an advanced lightweight technical filament designed for functional applications where both weight and mechanical flexibility are important.
This balance makes LW-PET FLEX particularly suitable for lightweight functional components that need to bend and absorb mechanical loads without failing through brittle fracture .
LW-PET FLEX NATURAL is particularly suitable for parts where weight reduction without excessive brittleness is important.

Potential applications include drones, RC components, protective structures, lightweight enclosures, wearable components, damping structures and other functional parts exposed to bending, vibration or occasional impacts.

It is also an interesting choice for larger lightweight designs where conventional rigid materials would add unnecessary mass and very soft flexible materials would provide insufficient structural stability.
LW-PET FLEX NATURAL is a lightweight filament developed for functional parts that require a balance of flexibility, toughness and structural stability.
Mechanical behaviour: Tough, flexible and impact-resistant
It offers a useful balance between strength, toughness and controlled flexibility.
Active foaming technology enables the production of lightweight parts with a lower density.
Compared with conventional rigid materials, LW-PET FLEX offers greater flexibility and improved resistance to impact and deformation .
At the same time, it retains considerably more structural stability than very soft flexible filaments.
During extrusion, the material can expand, increasing its volume and reducing the density of the printed part.
This allows significant weight savings compared with printing the same geometry without expansion.
Its expanding behaviour during printing reduces part density and makes it possible to produce lightweight components with adjustable mechanical properties.
The result is a versatile technical filament that combines low weight, flexibility, impact resistance and easy printability .
The degree of expansion can be influenced through settings such as temperature, printing speed and material flow .
Reducing density through foaming can also change the mechanical behaviour of a printed part.
As expansion increases and density decreases, parts can become lighter and more compliant under load .

The material can therefore be adapted to different applications: print at a higher density when additional structural stability is required, or increase expansion when lower weight and greater flexibility are more important.

items.text: All thermoplastic polyester resins will hydrolyze in hot water. The hydrolysis results in polymer degradation and a decrease in the physical properties of the resin. The rate of hydrolysis depends on exposure conditions; primarily time, temperature and the composition of the specific polyester resin. We recommend that parts made from Rynite should not be used in an environment where there is continuous exposure to water at temperatures above 50 °C.

items.agent: Outdoor weathering (carbon arc X-W Weather-Ometer, Florida and Arizona exposure)
items.text: Thermoplastic polyester resins rank high, among engineering polymers, for resistance to outdoor weathering... in general, Rynite exhibits good property retention. Overall performance is improved, especially impact strength, by the addition of carbon black (> 0,3 % by weight) to the resin. After 10 000 hours in the X-W Weather-Ometer Rynite 530 NC010 and Rynite 545 NC010 retain over 70 % of their initial tensile strength and 55 % of their original elongation properties.
